result.topic_en: The page finishes an argument about the forms of divisors (showing a proposition false via primes 2p+1 dividing 2^p+1), lists values of x for which 17, 41, 73, 89 divide x^4+1, and begins a section on quadratic residues with a conjectured theorem and theorems to be demonstrated about residues modulo primes 4n+1 and 4n-1.

d) De divisoribus et residuis numerorum quadratorum.
19.
Theorema, cujus demonstratio desideratur.
Si pro divisore $d$ inter residua quadratorum occurrat $\pm r$, tum etiam pro divisore $4nr+d$, si fuerit numerus primus, inter residua quadratorum idem quoque residuum $\pm r$ occurret. Ita si sit $d=7$, inter residua quadratorum occurrit 2; ideoque quoties $8n+7$ fuerit numerus primus, (eo divisore) inter residua quadratorum reperiatur 2 necesse est.
Ratio in eo quaerenda videtur, quod si $8n+7$ est numerus primus, tum numerus residuorum semper est $4n+3$, dum si non fuerit primus, multitudo residuorum multo est minor: scilicet pro $8n+7=15$, multitudo residuorum non est 7, sed tantum 5.
A. m. T. I. p. 210.
20.
Theoremata demonstranda.
I. Si per numerum primum $4n+1$ omnia quadrata dividantur, inter residua occurret non solum ipse numerus $n$, sed etiam omnes ejus divisores et quidem singuli utroque signo affecti.
II. Si per numerum primum $4n-1$ omnia quadrata dividantur, inter residua non solum occurret ipse numerus $n$, sed etiam omnes ejus divisores signo $+$ affecti; iidem enim signo $-$ affecti erunt non-residua.
Haec duo theoremata ita generalius proponi possunt: Denotante $i$ numerum imparem quemcunque,
I. si per numerum primum $4n+ii$ quadrata dividantur, inter residua occurrent omnes divisores numeri $n$, tam signo $+$ quam signo $-$ affecti.

items.quote: Neque vero propositio supra memorata est vera, plures enim casus assignari possunt, quibus fallit.
items.english: But the proposition mentioned above is not true, for several cases can be given in which it fails.

items.quote: Si pro divisore $d$ inter residua quadratorum occurrat $\pm r$, tum etiam pro divisore $4nr+d$, si fuerit numerus primus, inter residua quadratorum idem quoque residuum $\pm r$ occurret.
items.english: If for divisor d the residue ±r occurs among the residues of squares, then also for divisor 4nr+d, if it is prime, the same residue ±r will occur among the residues of squares.

items.quote: Ratio in eo quaerenda videtur, quod si $8n+7$ est numerus primus, tum numerus residuorum semper est $4n+3$
items.english: The reason seems to be sought in the fact that if 8n+7 is prime, the number of residues is always 4n+3.

items.quote: I. Si per numerum primum $4n+1$ omnia quadrata dividantur, inter residua occurret non solum ipse numerus $n$, sed etiam omnes ejus divisores et quidem singuli utroque signo affecti.
items.english: If all squares are divided by a prime 4n+1, among the residues will occur not only n itself but also all its divisors, each with both signs.

items.quote: II. Si per numerum primum $4n-1$ omnia quadrata dividantur, inter residua non solum occurret ipse numerus $n$, sed etiam omnes ejus divisores signo $+$ affecti; iidem enim signo $-$ affecti erunt non-residua.
items.english: If all squares are divided by a prime 4n-1, among the residues will occur not only n but all its divisors with sign +; the same with sign - will be non-residues.

items.quote: I. si per numerum primum $4n+ii$ quadrata dividantur, inter residua occurrent omnes divisores numeri $n$, tam signo $+$ quam signo $-$ affecti.
items.english: If squares are divided by a prime 4n+i² (i odd), all divisors of n, with both + and - signs, will occur among the residues.
